ADJOURNMENT CITY COUNCIL

 agenda item being considered, the public hearing or non-public hearing agenda item will automatically be
 continued to the next regularly scheduled City Council meeting. If you will require special accommodations, due
 to a disability, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (310) 412-5280 or FAX (310) 412-5533, One
 Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301. All requests for special
 accommodations must be received 72 hours prior to the day of the Council Meetings.

Inglewood, California
  November 26, 2019

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
Tuesday, November 26, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

APPOINTMENT OF MAYOR PRO TEM. It was moved by Council Member
Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the City Council does
hereby appoint Council Member Morales as Mayor Pro Tem for closed session.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Franklin;
Noes: None; and
Absent: Mayor Butts.
Mayor Pro Tem Morales called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour
of 1:03 p.m.
The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Pro Tem Morales, Council Members Dotson,
  Padilla, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  Mayor Butts.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor
Pro Tem Morales inquired if there were any persons present who wished to
address the City Council on the Closed Session Item.

There was no response.

Mayor Pro Tem Morales recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:04 p.m. for
Closed Session Item CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
Authority, Finance Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at
the hour of 2:00 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority
Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority  Chairman/Finance  Authority
  Chairman/Parking  Authority  Chairman/Joint
  Powers Authority Chairman Butts, Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority  Members/Finance  Authority
  Members/Parking  Authority  Members/Joint
  Powers Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

  1
 November 26, 2019

  City/Successor Agency / Housing Authority / Finance Authority / Parking
  Authority /Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
  Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking
  Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there
  were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers
  Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

 180  PRESENTATION – RECOGNITION OF REPUBLIC SERVICES
  SUPERVISOR CEDRIC “CJ” GRIFFIN, JR. The City Council recognized
  Mr. Cedric “CJ” Griffin, Jr. for his outstanding service to the City of Inglewood.

  Mr. Cedric “CJ” Griffin, Jr., thanked the City Council for the honor.

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Padilla, and seconded
  by Council Member /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member
  Morales that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated, November 22, 2019, in the amount of
  $3,262,896.44, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor
  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending
  the following:
  A. Rejection of the following claim filed pursuant to Government Code
  Section 913:
  1) Magdalena Rodriguez for alleged personal injury on September 10, 2019.
  B. Rejection of the following insufficient claims filed pursuant to
  Government Code Section 913:
  1) Gloria Flucas for alleged vehicle damage on June 14, 2019.
  2) LaTanya Wheeler for alleged personal injury on October 5, 2019.
  C. Return of the following late claim filed pursuant to Government Code
  Section 911.2:
  1) Alliance United Insurance subro Edwin Arroyo-Marroquin for alleged vehicle
  damage on December 19, 2018.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, seconded by Council Member
  Morales, that the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject the claims filed by
  Magdalena Rodriguez, Gloria Flucas, and LaTanya Wheeler; and 2) Return the
  late claim filed by Alliance United Insurance subro Edwin Arroyo-Marroquin.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and

  2
 November 26, 2019

  `  Noes: None.
125  RESOLUTION NO. 20-19 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2019-2020 ANNUAL BUDGET TO SECURE VARIOUS LEGAL
  SERVICES. Staff report dated November 26, 2019, was presented
  recommending adoption of a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2019-2020
  annual budget transferring $500,000 from General Fund Reserves to secure
  various legal services.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that Resolution No. 20-19 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AMENDING THE 2019-2020 ANNUAL
  BUDGET TO ADD FUNDING FOR VARIOUS LEGAL
  SERVICES

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 125  AGREEMENT NO. 20-054 APPROVED – OLIVAREZ MADRUGA
  LEMIEUX O’NEILL, LLP. Staff report dated November 26, 2019, was
  presented recommending approval of an Agreement with Olivarez Madruga
  Lemieux O’Neill, LLP for broad ranging legal advice, guidance and
  representation.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 20-054 in the
  amount of $100,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 125  PAYMENT OF OUTSTANDING INVOICES AUTHORIZED – HARRIS &
  ASSOCIATES; AGREEMENT NO. 20-055 APPROVED. Staff report dated
  November 26, 2019, was presented recommending approval of an Agreement
  with Harris & Associates for broad ranging legal advice, guidance and
  representation.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Authorize payment of outstanding
  invoices from Harris & Associates for legal services rendered in the amount of
  $65,000; and 2) Approve Agreement No. 20-055 in the amount of $100,000. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by
  Council Member Morales that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on
  October 29, 2019, and November 5, 2019, and the Special Council Meeting held
  on November 14, 2019, be approved. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 101  PAYMENT OF OUTSTANDING INVOICES AUTHORIZED – IT’S YOUR
  PARTY. Staff report dated November 26, 2019, was presented recommending
  authorization to pay outstanding invoices submitted by It’s Your Party Floral &
  Event Design (It’s Your Party).

  3
 November 26, 2019

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Authorize payment in the amount
  of $5,557.40; and 2) Authorize staff to continue with the services of It’s Your
  Party for the completion of the event planning tasks already underway for the
  2019 Holiday Tree Lighting Event, and the 37th Annual Dr. Martin Luther King,
  Jr., Commemorative Service and Celebration – King Fest in an amount up to
  $20,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 301  RESOLUTION NO. 20-20 ADOPTED – AUTHORIZING THE CITY
  MANAGER OR HIS DESIGNEE TO SUBMIT AN APPLICATION FOR
  RECEIPT OF SB2 PLANNING GRANT PROGRAM FUNDS. Staff report
  dated November 26, 2019, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution
  authorizing the City Manager or his designee to submit an application for receipt
  of SB2 Planning Grants Program Funds to update the City’s Housing Element.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 20-20
  entitled:
  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,  AUTHORIZING  THE  CITY
  MANAGER OR HIS DESIGNEE TO SUBMIT AN APPLICATION TO
  THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA FOR SB 2 PLANNING GRANTS
  PROGRAM FUNDS, AND IF THE APPLICATION IS APPROVED,
  AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO SIGN AN AGREEMENT AND
  ANY OTHER DOCUMENT NECESSARY TO SECURE THE GRANT
  FUNDS
  and; 2) Authorize the Mayor to sign an agreement and any other documentation
  necessary to secure the grant funds, upon approval of the application. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 142  AGREEMENT NO. 20-056 APPROVED – ARAMARK; PAYMENT OF
  OUTSTANDING AND ADDITIONAL INVOICES APPROVED. Staff report
  dated November 26, 2019, was presented recommending approval of a one-year
  and eight-month agreement (with the option to extend two additional one year
  terms) with Aramark, to provide garments, towels, mats, and mops for City
  employees.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 20-056 in
  the annual amount of $114,500; 2) Approve payment of outstanding invoices in
  the amount of $6,789.01; and 3) Authorize staff to pay additional invoices up to
  $12,000 for services utilized prior to contract approval. The motion was carried
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  4
 November 26, 2019

 178  AGREEMENT NO. 20-057 APPROVED – THREE-YEAR AGREEMENT
  WITH PHAMATECH, INC. Staff report dated November 26, 2019, was
  presented recommending approval of a three-year agreement (with the option to
  extend an additional year) with Phamatech, Inc., to provide laboratory testing and
  urine sample collection services for pre-employment and random drug screenings,
  per Bid No. RFB-0113.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 20-057 in the
  annual amount of $20,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 132.6  CLOSED SESSION – CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL;
  XOCHIL TORRES, ET AL V. CITY OF INGLEWOOD. Closed session –
  Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged; Conference with Legal Counsel
  regarding Pending Litigation Pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(1); Name of Case: Xochil Torres, et al v. City of Inglewood, et al.;
  LASC Case No.: 19TRCV00065.

  Discussion held; Direction given to staff.

 101  ORAL REPORTS – CITY MANAGER. Artie Fields, City Manager, stated that
  the Parks and Recreation survey was a success and thanked everyone who
  participated. He stated that the winner of the survey was a resident of District 2.
  Mr. Fields also introduced Lisa Trifiletti of Trifiletti Consulting who presented a
  PowerPoint presentation on the progress of the Inglewood Transit Procurement
  Project Delivery approach.

 127  ORAL REPORTS – CITY CLERK. Yvonne Horton, City Clerk, stated her and
  Aisha Thompson, Deputy City Clerk, attended Maxine Waters community
  meeting held on Saturday, November 23, 2019. She also stated that the County
  Registrar-Recorder’s Office will be in her office with the new Voter Solutions
  device the first week of December, and invited everyone to try out the new
  machine and also give their feedback.

 219  ORAL REPORTS – CITY TREASURER. Wanda Brown, City Treasurer gave
  a brief report on the bonds and cd’s she purchased on behalf of the city.
  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Eric Holly commented the turkey giveaway went great. He invited everyone to
  attend the Chambers gala on December 12, 2019, at the Renaissance Hotel from
  6:00 p.m. until 12:00 a.m.

  Willie Agee wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving.

  Elle Gonzalez inquired how she would go about opening a massage therapy
  business in Inglewood on Market Street.

  Ray Davis wished everyone happy holidays, and commented that he hopes to see
  everyone next year.

  5
 November 26, 2019

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the
  meeting adjourned at the hour of 2:24 p.m.

  Approved this 10th day of December, 2019

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
